<!-- 1:40–1:45 -->
```{r}
#| label: easystats-data
#| include: false
# The country-year panel under the name that the webR workspace and the modules give it, for
# the two slides of code behind the menu
europeanisation <- readr::read_csv("../data/europeanisation_cy.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## The data work {#the-data-work .smaller}

::: {.small}
The code behind the menu is the data half of **easystats**, the verbs of datawizard. Each line below runs in the webR workspace, in the pipeline or in one of the workshop's modules, and its comment says where:
:::

::: {.fs-75}
```r
# a sample: the country-years without an assistance programme (module Causal graphs)
datawizard::data_filter(europeanisation, bailout == 0)
# the predictor centred, as C6HJR centred it (webR workspace, Task 3)
europeanisation <- datawizard::data_modify(europeanisation, unemp_c = unemp - mean(unemp))
# the scale variant of 018OL, the cell means rescaled to 0–1 (webR workspace, Task 3)
o18ol <- datawizard::data_modify(o18ol, pos01 = datawizard::rescale(pos, to = c(0, 1)))
# cell means from the respondents (pipeline, R/15_analyst_panels.R)
kqxue_resp |>
  datawizard::data_summary(cosmo = mean(cosmo), n = length(cosmo), by = c("cntry", "year"))
# claim alignment, the sign of a growth slope reversed (module R on the country-year panel)
curve |> datawizard::data_modify(r_ca = dplyr::if_else(predictor == "growth", -r, r))
# the country mean of unemployment and the departure of each year from it (module Panel data)
europeanisation_wb <- datawizard::demean(europeanisation, select = "unemp", by = "cntry")
```
:::

::: {.small}
- One framework from the data to the models: the frame that `demean()` returns goes straight into `lmer()`, and `parameters::model_parameters()` reads the fit
- The verbs keep the variable labels of a survey file as it arrives from the archive, so a labelled Eurobarometer file stays labelled through the chain
- The help page of a verb names the methods behind it: `demean()` cites Bell and Jones (2015) and Bell, Fairbrother and Jones (2019) for the within–between split
:::

::: {.src}
@LudeckeEtAl2022EasystatsFrameworkEasy; @BellJones2015ExplainingFixedEffects; @BellEtAl2019FixedRandomEffects.
:::

::: notes
These two slides show code, although they are not a lesson in R. The workshop does its data work with datawizard, the data half of the easystats framework, and the six lines on the slide are copied from the places where they run: a filter for a sample, a new column for the centred predictor and another for the rescaled outcome of 018OL, cell means from the respondents, grouped by country and year as in the rebuilt panel of KQXUE, claim alignment, which reverses the sign of a growth slope, and `demean()`, which returns the country mean of unemployment and the departure of each year from it in one call, the two columns of the within–between model. Of the three points at the foot of the slide, the second matters most for survey data, I think, since a labelled Eurobarometer file keeps its labels through the whole chain.
:::

## Reading a model {#reading-a-model .smaller}

::: {.fs-70}
```{r}
#| label: reading-a-model-fit
#| echo: true
#| message: false
# the reproduced specification (module Panel data), read as Task 3 of the webR workspace prints it
m_twfe <- fixest::feols(mcosmo ~ unemp | cntry + year, data = europeanisation, vcov = "iid")
print(parameters::model_parameters(m_twfe), digits = 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: reading-a-model-cr2
#| echo: true
#| message: false
# the CR2 test that classes every point of the curve, on the dummy-variable fit (module Panel data)
m_lsdv <- lm(mcosmo ~ unemp + factor(cntry) + factor(year), data = europeanisation)
clubSandwich::coef_test(m_lsdv, vcov = "CR2", cluster = europeanisation$cntry, coefs = "unemp",
                        test = "Satterthwaite")
```

```{r}
#| label: reading-a-model-r
#| echo: true
# the conversion rule of the robustness study, r = t / sqrt(t^2 + df), as one call (background page, section 4)
effectsize::t_to_r(-3.804, 233)
```
:::

::: {.src}
@LudeckeEtAl2020ExtractingComputingExploring; @BellMcCaffrey2002BiasReductionStandard; @PustejovskyTipton2018SmallsampleMethodsClusterrobust; the conversion rule of @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness (`standard_correlation_coefficient.R` in marton-balazs-kovacs/multi100 on GitHub).
:::

::: notes
Reading a model is the other half of easystats. The parameters package reads any fitted model into one table, printed here with five digits so that you can compare the t with the value on record, minus three point eight on two hundred and thirty-three degrees of freedom. The second block is the test that classes every point of the curve, one call to clubSandwich on the dummy-variable fit, with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, fewer than ten here, and a p just above point zero five; the parameters package can ask for CR2 errors too, but tests them on the residual degrees of freedom. The conversion used by the robustness study is one call to effectsize, with the degrees of freedom as its second argument, and the open circle of PRL47 comes from the rule for a z statistic, which takes the number of respondents in place of the degrees of freedom.
:::
